MRK.rationale: Merck presents a fundamentally sound franchise temporarily obscured by a large one-time acquisition charge. Q1 2026 GAAP results were deeply negative (net loss -$4.24B, operating income -$3.53B) but this is almost certainly driven by the $9.0B Cidara acquisition write-down — revenue grew 4.9% YoY to $16.29B, gross margins held at ~74%, and operating cash flow remained solid at $3.92B in the same quarter. The underlying business engine is intact: Keytruda grew 11.5% YoY to $8.03B, Animal Health accelerated +13%, and multiple new launches (Welireg +45%, PREVYMIS +31%) are gaining traction. On normalized earnings (~$2.00/quarter, $8.00 annualized), the stock at $115.88 trades at ~14.5x, within the historical 11-16x range and offering a ~6.9% earnings yield well above the 10-year Treasury at 4.57%. Full-year adjusted EPS guidance was raised to ~$5.10 midpoint, implying ~22.7x on adjusted forward earnings — reasonable for a large-cap pharma with this franchise quality. The Keytruda patent cliff (late 2028-2029) remains the dominant structural risk, but the Qlex subcutaneous conversion strategy, pipeline diversification (Cidara, Terns $5.7B acquisition, Erasca collaboration), and $3B cost-cutting initiative provide credible mitigation. Regeneron's Phase 3 melanoma trial failure (May 18) removes a near-term competitive threat to Keytruda. The score is capped at mildly attractive rather than higher because: (1) the Q1 charge nature is not yet fully clarified from filings, (2) Gardasil's structural decline adds to the post-Keytruda revenue gap, (3) the 5-year EPS decline of 1.3% annually despite 8.8% revenue growth raises questions about incremental profitability, and (4) P/B at 6.237x is at the ceiling of its historical range. A modest positive catalyst exists in the upcoming quarters as the market digests adjusted earnings recovery and pipeline progress.
